demo_tour_keys: Use the left and right arrow keys to move between steps, Escape to close.
demo_tour_s1_body: The overview reads like a forecast: one sentence for the whole estate, and below it only the things worth your attention. A quiet sky means you can close the tab.
demo_tour_s1_title: The weather, then what needs you
demo_tour_s2_body: This Proxmox cluster shows nodes, guests, storage, replication and backups on one page, from the same API the real collector reads. Every chart has the last seven days.
demo_tour_s3_body: Rules come ready-made. A switch that goes down silences everything behind it; seasonal baselines learn what a normal Tuesday looks like; forecasts warn a disk will fill before it does.
demo_tour_s4_body: Email, ntfy, Matrix, Discord, Slack, Telegram, Gotify, webhooks and more — with quiet hours and per-device overrides. The demo never sends anything.
demo_tour_s5_body: Pick a type from the catalogue — hypervisors, NAS, firewalls, servers, printers, websites — and the form asks only for what that type needs. SNMP devices are recognised on their own.
demo_tour_s6_body: One small binary for Linux and Windows pushes CPU, disks, services and containers. It can also relay probes from a remote site that the server cannot reach.
demo_tour_s7_body: Publish a public page for your users, with incidents, uptime badges and email subscriptions — without exposing the rest of the instance.
demo_tour_s8_body: For a screen in the room: the bulletin full screen, readable from across it, with an optional music player. That is the tour — look around, nothing you click can break.

deviceform_enroll_intro: A server with the agent has no address to enter: the agent installed on the machine introduces itself to this server. Create a token, run the command it gives you, done.
deviceform_enroll_origin_note: The commands below point the agent at {origin}, the address of this page. If the site reaches this server at another address — usually a public HTTPS name — replace it before running them.
deviceform_enroll_relay_intro: A relay is an ordinary agent with one more setting. Placed on a machine at another site — a second office, a client, a VPS — it runs this server's probes from there and sends back the results. It only connects out: no port to open, no VPN.

deviceform_enroll_step3: Add the devices of that site
deviceform_enroll_step3_note: The relay appears among the devices within a minute. Add each switch, NAS or hypervisor there as usual, with its address as seen from the site, and under More options set "Reached through" to the relay. Nothing needs opening at the site: the relay only connects out.

deviceform_feature_backups_next: Install the agent on a machine that can open the repositories, then list them under “restic_repos:” or “borg_repos:” in its agent.yaml, with a password file. The password never leaves the machine.
deviceform_feature_backups_summary: Age of the last snapshot of each repository, and whether it can still be read.
deviceform_feature_disks_next: The agent reads SMART with smartctl: install smartmontools on the machine. The installed service has the rights it needs; sleeping disks are never woken.
deviceform_feature_disks_summary: Wear, reallocated and pending sectors, temperature: a drive warns weeks before it fails.
deviceform_feature_docker_next: The agent reads the containers from the Docker socket. Install it on the machine that runs Docker: they appear on that machine’s page.
deviceform_feature_docker_summary: State, health, restarts and image updates of every container, with restart and update from here.
deviceform_feature_hyperv_next: Install the agent on the Hyper-V host (Windows Server or Windows with the Hyper-V role): it finds the vmms service and reads Hyper-V’s performance counters on its own. The Hyper-V panel appears on that machine’s page.
deviceform_feature_hyperv_summary: Virtual machines in critical health, the host’s real CPU load with its guests, memory of each VM and virtual disk errors.
deviceform_feature_plakar_next: The agent finds Plakar and its klosets on its own. Install it on the machine that runs the backups: the Backups panel appears on its page.
deviceform_feature_plakar_summary: Age, count and state of the snapshots in each kloset, found without any setup.
deviceform_feature_relay_next: Install the agent on any machine at the remote site, then switch it to relay mode. Add the devices of that site as usual, with their local address, and pick the agent under More options → Reached through.
deviceform_feature_relay_summary: An agent at a second site, a client’s office or behind a NAT probes the devices there for this server. Outbound only.
deviceform_feature_sensors_next: The agent reads the probes the system exposes, on Linux, macOS and FreeBSD; fan speeds on Linux only. Windows exposes none.
deviceform_feature_sensors_summary: The machine’s own temperature probes against their critical point, and fan speeds.
deviceform_feature_services_next: Install the agent, then name the services to watch under “services:” in its agent.yaml. Failed systemd units are reported without any list.
deviceform_feature_services_summary: systemd units, Windows services, launchd and rc.d services, running or stopped.
deviceform_feature_updates_next: The agent reads them with dnf or apt, on Fedora, RHEL, Debian and Ubuntu families.
deviceform_feature_updates_summary: Pending and security updates, a reboot waiting, failed units, SELinux mode.
deviceform_feature_wireguard_next: The agent reads the tunnels with wg show, on Linux: install it on the machine that runs WireGuard. Peers with a persistent keepalive alert when they go silent.
deviceform_feature_wireguard_summary: Every peer of every interface: time since its last handshake, traffic, and tunnels gone silent.
deviceform_feature_zfs_next: The agent reads the pools with zpool, on Linux, FreeBSD or TrueNAS. Install it on the machine that holds them.
deviceform_feature_zfs_summary: Pool state, fill, device errors and the age of the last scrub.

notifications_policy_cap_help: Past the cap, alerts wait and arrive as one digest. Empty: no cap.

notifications_policy_escalate_off: Nobody is told twice: an alert nobody acknowledges keeps to its own channels.
notifications_policy_escalate_on: If nobody acknowledges within {minutes} min of the first message going out, the alert is also sent to {name} — once. Acknowledging it, or its clearing, stops the hop.
notifications_policy_flap_help: An alert that fires and clears repeatedly sends one “flapping” notice, then stays silent for a while.
notifications_policy_group_help: Alerts that fire within this window leave as one message per channel: “3 alerts on 2 devices”.
notifications_policy_per_channel_note: What each channel hears, and its quiet hours, are set on the channel itself (Edit, then “Delivery options”).
notifications_policy_url_help: Used for the “Open in DumbMonit” link in every message. Leave empty to use DUMBMONIT_PUBLIC_URL.

notifications_quiet_help: Only Warning-level alerts come through during quiet hours; the rest waits and arrives as one digest when they end.

overview_tip_agent_text: Services, disk health, temperatures, updates waiting, Docker containers you can restart or update from here, Plakar, restic and Borg backups. One command on Linux, Windows, macOS or FreeBSD.
overview_tip_agent_title: The agent sees inside a machine.
overview_tip_api_text: A scoped token (read, or read and write) opens it to your scripts, and a Prometheus or Grafana you already run can read the measurements with the same token.
overview_tip_api_title: Everything here has an HTTP API.
overview_tip_mcp_text: Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any MCP client can ask DumbMonit how things are — and, with a write token, silence a device or run a probe.
overview_tip_mcp_title: An AI assistant can read this bulletin.
overview_tip_packs_text: An integration pack is a device type written in YAML: what to ask the device, which numbers to keep, when to alert.
overview_tip_packs_title: DumbMonit can learn a new device.
overview_tip_palette_text: The command palette jumps to any device, page or action without leaving the keyboard.
overview_tip_palette_title: Every page and action is one shortcut away.
overview_tip_relay_text: Put one on a machine at a second site, a client’s office or behind a NAT: it probes the switches, NAS and hypervisors there for this server. Outbound only — nothing to open on that side.
overview_tip_relay_title: An agent can watch another network.
overview_tip_status_text: A public status page shows the services you pick, their uptime and your announcements — a link to share instead of answering “is it down?”.
overview_tip_wall_text: Wall mode shows the sky and what needs you, full screen and readable across the room, and keeps the screen awake.
overview_week_quiet: A quiet week ahead: no certificate, disk or maintenance due.

settings_agents_description: An agent is one small program on a Linux, Windows, macOS or FreeBSD machine: it reports the system, disks, services, Docker containers and backups, and lets you restart or update a container from here. In relay mode it also probes, for this server, the devices of its own network — a second site, a client, anything behind a NAT — and only ever connects out.
settings_agents_empty_description: Create one, then run the install command on the machine.
settings_agents_expires_help: Days. Machines already enrolled keep reporting; leave empty for no deadline.
settings_agents_machines_invalid: The number of machines must be a whole number, one or more.
settings_agents_name_required: Name the token, for example after the machine it will enrol.
settings_agents_new_token_help: Only used to recognise the token in this list.
settings_agents_none: No agent has reported to this server yet.
settings_agents_relay_off_title: Set relay: true on this agent so it picks up their probes

settings_agents_reusable_help: Off, the token enrols one machine and then enrols nothing more — the right default for a single install. On, it can go into a playbook or an image.
settings_agents_spent_note: Machines enrolled with it keep reporting; it just cannot let a new one in.
settings_agents_tokens_intro: Adding a device of type agent makes a single-use token for you. Create one here for a fleet, a playbook or a machine image.
settings_appearance_description: Both themes are first-class. System follows your device and switches with it.
settings_appearance_wall_description: The bulletin alone, full screen, for a monitor in the room. Press Esc to leave; ⌘K / Ctrl K opens it from anywhere.
settings_assistant_chatgpt_https_warning: This page is not served over HTTPS: put DumbMonit behind a reverse proxy with TLS before exposing it.
settings_assistant_chatgpt_text: In ChatGPT, open Settings → Connectors → Create (developer mode), then fill in the MCP server URL and the authorization header. ChatGPT connects from OpenAI's servers, so the URL must be reachable from the internet over HTTPS.
settings_assistant_created_note: The snippets below now carry this token. Treat it like a password.
settings_assistant_cursor_text: Cursor (.cursor/mcp.json) and most other MCP clients accept this shape — a Streamable HTTP server with a bearer header:
settings_assistant_description: One kind of token for both: let Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any MCP client ask DumbMonit how things are, or call the REST API from a script. A read token can only look; a write token can also change things — silence a device, run a probe, add or edit devices, rules and channels.
settings_assistant_desktop_text: Add to claude_desktop_config.json (Settings → Developer → Edit Config), then restart Claude Desktop. It needs Node.js: mcp-remote bridges the desktop app to this server.
settings_assistant_empty_description: Create one above, then paste the snippet into your assistant or script.
settings_assistant_expires_help: An expired token stops working; create a new one then.
settings_assistant_http_warning: This page is served over plain HTTP, so the snippet includes --allow-http. Keep that to your own network.
settings_assistant_mcp_note: The server speaks MCP over Streamable HTTP, without sessions. Every client, the tools and the security notes:
settings_assistant_name_required: Name the token, for example after the assistant or the machine it runs on.
settings_assistant_networks_help: Optional. Addresses or CIDR ranges, separated by commas or spaces. Empty: usable from anywhere.
settings_assistant_new_token_help: Only used to recognise the token in this list.
settings_assistant_openapi_note: The OpenAPI file loads in Swagger UI, Postman or Insomnia, and generates clients. Calls from another web origin work with a bearer token only, never with a session.
settings_assistant_prometheus_text: A Prometheus or Grafana you already run can read this instance with a read token — /metrics for the server's own health, /federate for the measurements, /prometheus as a Grafana data source: see

settings_assistant_prompt_silence: Silence the NAS for two hours
settings_assistant_rest_text: The same token opens the REST API to scripts and dashboards: send it as a bearer header instead of a session cookie — no anti-CSRF header needed. A read token maps to a viewer, a write token to an administrator, except that no token can manage accounts, sign-in settings, tokens or backups.

settings_backup_accounts_help: Off by default. Without them, restored accounts exist but cannot sign in until an administrator sets a password.
settings_backup_admin_only_description: A backup holds every credential of this instance.
settings_backup_admin_only_title: Only an administrator can export or restore.
settings_backup_description: Export this instance as one encrypted file, restore it onto a fresh one, and keep a daily copy of the database next to it.
settings_backup_downloaded: Downloaded — keep the passphrase with it
settings_backup_export_excluded: Not included: metrics history, alert state and history, the audit log, open sessions — and the instance secret, on purpose.
settings_backup_export_intro: One file, format version {version}. It contains every credential of this instance in a form the passphrase alone protects: store it where you store passwords, not next to the backups of your films.
settings_backup_not_backup: This file is not a DumbMonit backup.
settings_backup_not_json: This file could not be read as JSON. Pick the bundle you downloaded.
settings_backup_passphrase_help: At least {min} characters. There is no way to recover a bundle whose passphrase is lost.
settings_backup_passphrase_mismatch: The two passphrases do not match. Type the confirmation again.
settings_backup_passphrase_short: At least {min} characters. Three words is enough, and you will need them again to restore.
settings_backup_read_error: Could not read the backup state
settings_backup_restore_intro: Checked first, applied only if you ask. Restoring never deletes anything: it creates what is missing and updates what differs, matching devices on their kind and address. Accounts that already exist here are left untouched.
settings_backup_schedule_env_secret: The secret comes from the environment, so it is not copied here.
settings_backup_schedule_intro_key: An online, consistent copy of the database is written to {directory}, with a copy of secret.key beside it.
settings_backup_schedule_intro_nokey: An online, consistent copy of the database is written to {directory}.
settings_backup_schedule_same_volume: They live in the same volume as the database: they undo a mistake, not a lost disk.
settings_backup_secret_bundle: The bundle below is the exception: its secrets are re-encrypted with the passphrase you choose, so it restores onto a fresh instance that has its own secret.
settings_backup_secret_env: This server reads its secret from DUMBMONIT_SECRET, so there is no file to copy. Keep that value in your password manager: without it, a copy of the database restores an instance that cannot talk to anything.
settings_backup_secret_file: Device passwords, SNMP communities and channel secrets are encrypted with a key derived from {path}. A copy of the database without that file restores an instance that cannot talk to anything — and the server refuses to start rather than pretend otherwise. Back it up with the database.
settings_backup_secret_title: The instance secret is what decrypts your credentials
settings_music_admin_only: An admin can connect a Spotify account here.
settings_music_connect_intro: The wall becomes a speaker named {name}: in the Spotify app on your phone, open Devices and pick it, the sound comes out of the display. The wall also shows what plays on the account wherever it plays — the TV's app, a cast speaker, your laptop.
settings_music_description: Start music from your phone and hear it on the wall display, or send it a Spotify, Deezer or YouTube link.
settings_music_err_client_id: Paste the Client ID from your app’s page in the Spotify Developer Dashboard (32 letters and digits).

settings_music_link_intro: Without Premium, or for Deezer and YouTube — which have no Connect-style remote on the web — send a link from any screen, your phone included: every wall plays it in the service's own player. A browser not signed in to Spotify or Deezer on the wall plays 30-second previews.

settings_music_needs_2: The phone must be signed in to the same Spotify account as the one connected here: a browser speaker is only listed for its own account — not for other members of a Family plan, and not found on the network like a smart speaker.
settings_music_needs_3: For the wall to be a speaker, its browser must open DumbMonit over HTTPS (or as localhost on the display itself) and have working DRM (Widevine): Chrome, Edge or Firefox on a computer, Chromium with Widevine on a Raspberry Pi. Most smart-TV and kiosk browsers cannot — the wall says so on screen, and the walls below show it here.
settings_music_needs_4: Browsers keep a page silent until it is touched: tap or press a key on the wall once after it loads (or start the kiosk browser with --autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required).
settings_music_needs_5: “Now playing” works without any of that: the server asks Spotify what plays, every few seconds, even over plain HTTP.
settings_music_needs_6: Spotify ends a connection six months after it was approved: connect again before the date shown.

settings_music_reconnect_note: Spotify ends connections after six months.

settings_push_description: Alerts as native notifications on this phone or computer, even with DumbMonit closed. No app to install.
settings_push_enabled_notice: This device will receive push notifications. Send a test to check.
settings_push_help_channel: Which alerts arrive is decided by a Web Push channel in Alerts → Notifications.
settings_push_help_desktop_body: works in Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari. Installing the app (address bar → Install) is optional but keeps it one tap away.
settings_push_help_domains_body: the server sends to the browser vendor's push service, so it needs outbound HTTPS to fcm.googleapis.com (Chrome, Edge on Android), *.notify.windows.com (Edge), updates.push.services.mozilla.com (Firefox) and *.push.apple.com (Safari). settings_push_help_ios_body: open DumbMonit in Safari, Share → Add to Home Screen, open it from the Home Screen icon, then enable push here.

settings_push_text_https: Open DumbMonit over HTTPS (or on localhost) to enable push. This address is {origin}.
settings_push_text_install: On iPhone and iPad, add DumbMonit to the Home Screen (Share → Add to Home Screen), open it from there, then come back here.
settings_push_text_unsupported: This browser cannot receive push notifications. Try a recent Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari.

settings_report_dirty: Unsaved changes: save before sending a preview.

settings_update_data_kept: Your data lives in the /data volume and is kept. The page reloads itself once the server is back.
settings_update_off_releases: Check the releases page for new versions.

settings_users_no_disable_self: You cannot disable your own account.

status_action_confirm_lead: Press the button to receive incident and maintenance updates from this status page by email.

status_action_link_invalid: This link is no longer valid. Subscribe again from the status page.

status_action_unsub_lead: Press the button to stop receiving updates from this status page.

status_domain_step_proxy: In the proxy, send the name to the address of DumbMonit, for example {url}, without rewriting the path.
status_domain_what_body: Visitors who open this address see this status page straight away, at the root. Nothing else of DumbMonit answers there: no sign-in, no settings, no other page.
status_edit_description: Change what the page shows; visitors see it within a minute.
status_edit_new_description: Pick the services to show and the labels visitors will read. The page stays a draft until you publish it.
status_embed_not_found: This status page does not exist.
status_form_accent_help: Links, the top rule and the subscribe button. Each accent stays readable by day and by night.
status_form_description_help: One sentence under the title. Optional.
status_form_description_placeholder: What is up at home, at a glance.
status_form_domain_rule: The host name only, like status.example.com: no path, port or space.
status_form_footer_help: Plain text under the page, up to 280 characters: who runs it, how to reach them.
status_form_history_help: Longest window. The page shows as many days as its data covers, from 7 up to this.
status_form_homepage_help: Optional link shown next to the title.
status_form_logo_help: PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 256 KiB. Square works best.
status_form_logo_read: The file could not be read.
status_form_logo_size: The logo is limited to {kib} KiB.
status_form_logo_type: Use a PNG, JPEG or WebP image.
status_form_published_on: Anyone with the link can see it.
status_form_rotation_help: With several scenes ticked, which one a visitor sees and when it changes. They follow the order in which you ticked them.
status_form_scene_help: An optional illustrated city behind the title of the public page. New pages start on Paris; untick it for a plain page. Ignored in simple mode. Tick several to alternate between them.
status_form_services_empty: No device yet. Add one on the Devices page first.
status_form_services_help: Tick the devices to show. The label is what visitors read; a group heads a block of services.
status_form_simple_help: A plain page: no scene, no mascot, no animation. Light or dark follows the visitor's system, with a toggle.
status_form_slug_rule: 2 to 40 characters: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
status_form_subscribers_help: Visitors confirm their address by email, and every update carries a one-click unsubscribe link.
status_form_subscribers_no_channel: Add an email (SMTP) channel under Notifications to let visitors subscribe. Until then the page offers its RSS feed.
status_incidents_body_placeholder_mainte: Firmware upgrade on the router; expect a short outage.
status_incidents_empty_description: Open an incident when something breaks, or schedule a maintenance window ahead of time.
status_incidents_first_message_help: Optional. What visitors read under the title.
status_incidents_impact_major: Major — the page shows an outage
status_incidents_lead: Announcements shown at the top of a page — or of every page.
status_incidents_window_order: The end must come after the start.
status_incidents_window_required: A maintenance window needs a start and an end.
status_list_description: Public pages that show whether your services are up, with a 90-day history and your announcements. No sign-in needed to read them.
status_list_empty_description: Create one, pick the services to show, then share the link.
status_list_load_error: Could not load the status pages
status_list_pages_description: Each page shows only the services you put on it, under the labels you choose.
status_list_saved_draft: still a draft, visitors get a 404 until you publish it.

status_public_no_incident: No incident in the last 30 days.
status_public_no_service_description: This page has nothing to show for now.
status_public_not_found_description: Check the link you were given, or ask whoever runs this DumbMonit for the right one.
status_public_not_found_title: This status page does not exist.
status_share_description: Badges for a README and a compact view to embed in an intranet page.
status_share_embed_hint: Add {light} or {dark} to match the host page, {history} to hide the bars.
status_subscribers_empty_description: Visitors subscribe from the bottom of the public page.
status_updates_email_lead: An email when an incident or a maintenance is announced or changes. Unsubscribe from any message.
status_updates_rate_limited: Too many requests from here. Try again in a few minutes.
status_uptime_bar_label: {label}: uptime per day over {days} days. Use the arrow keys to move between days.
tips_alerts_clear_history: "Clear all resolved" sweeps the closed alerts out of your history in one go, once you are done reading them.
tips_alerts_ignore_device: A rule firing on a device that will just never comply? Ignore that rule for that one device — the rule still watches everywhere else.
tips_alerts_learning: A new baseline rule stays silent for its first 14 days: it is still learning what normal looks like for this device before it dares to alert on it.
tips_alerts_snooze: Snoozing an alert buys it a fixed window of quiet; it comes back on its own once that window ends — no need to remember to re-enable it.
tips_alerts_suppressed: An alert marked "suppressed" is not being ignored — its parent is already down, and I am not paging you twice for the same outage.
tips_device_docker: On an agent with Docker, you can restart or update a container from right here — no terminal required.
tips_device_probe_now: "Probe now" asks this device right now, live, instead of waiting for its next scheduled check — the fastest way to find out why it has gone quiet.
tips_device_secrets: Credentials never come back once saved. Editing this device without touching the password field just keeps the one already stored — nothing round-trips to your screen.
tips_device_silence: Expecting noise — a reboot, a firmware update? Silence this device for a while and its alerts stay quiet without disabling the checks themselves.
tips_device_timeline: The timeline below the faceplate is this device’s whole story: every alert that opened and closed on it, in order.
tips_devices_folders: Drag a device into a folder to group it — a site, a rack, a client. Double-click a folder’s name to rename it in place.
tips_devices_network_scan: Scanning the network finds what is already answering before you type a single IP address by hand.
tips_devices_parent_child: A VM or container under its hypervisor inherits trouble quietly: if the host is down, its guests are marked suppressed instead of each paging you separately.
tips_devices_rack_order: The rack sorts itself: trouble floats to the top, everything else keeps the order you gave it. Children sit indented under their parent, always.
tips_devices_relay_agent: An agent can watch a whole second network for you — a client’s office, a site behind a NAT — reporting home over an outbound connection only.
tips_general_about_me: I am a pigeon. I live in your monitoring tool. I have made my peace with this.
tips_general_docs: Longer explanations live on Read the Docs — this bulletin keeps its own screens short on purpose.
tips_general_palette_everywhere: The keyboard shortcut for the command palette still works even with the hint gone from the nav — Ctrl K, or ⌘K on a Mac.
tips_general_quiet_option: If I am more than you want, the × below puts me away for this visit — or tell me to stop for good and I will not bring it up again.
tips_general_security_score: Every device gets a security score from what it actually exposes — not a guess, a reading.
tips_overview_briefing: This page is a briefing, not a dashboard: a sky, "since you last looked" in sentences, and "needs you" as tiles. No device list here on purpose — that lives on Devices.
tips_overview_last_7_days: "Last 7 days" boils the week down to three numbers: how long everything stayed up, the quietest device, and the one that paged you the most. Petty, but fair.
tips_overview_palette_anywhere: Ctrl K or ⌘K opens the command palette from anywhere, even here, even mid-scroll. No menu diving required.
tips_overview_sky_weather: I live the weather with you up there: I nap on the wire on a quiet night, startle when something breaks, and loop in confetti once the sky clears. Try breaking something. (Please don’t.)
tips_overview_week_ahead: "The week ahead" shows what is due on its day — a maintenance window, a renewal. A quiet week shrinks to one line so it never begs for attention it does not need.
tips_settings_2fa: Two-factor authentication is one QR code away, right in Account & security — worth it for the one account that can see every credential on this server.
tips_settings_assistant: Claude, ChatGPT or any MCP client can read this bulletin — and with a write token, silence a device or run a probe for you.
tips_settings_backup: The backup bundle is encrypted, but it still holds every credential this server knows. Keep `/data/secret.key` as carefully as the bundle itself.
tips_settings_packs: A device type is just a YAML file — an integration pack. Install one to teach me a device I do not already know.
tips_settings_wall_appearance: Wall mode is tuned in Appearance — including an OLED-friendly night theme for a screen that never turns off.
tips_status_embed: Add `/embed` to a status page’s link and it drops into an iframe neatly — handy for an internal wiki or a company intranet.
tips_status_incidents: Posting an incident update here keeps everyone off your chat, politely. Maintenance windows show as planned, not as a surprise outage.
tips_status_public_page: A status page answers "is it down?" before anyone has to ask — pick the services, share the link, done.
tips_status_subscribe: Visitors can subscribe to a status page for email updates; the unsubscribe link in every one of those emails works without them signing in anywhere.
tips_status_theme_param: A status page accepts `?theme=light` or `?theme=dark` in its URL, so an embed can match the page that hosts it instead of guessing.
